title: Safe direction and the safety rules
subtitle: Where to point, and the four rules that always apply

lines: Welcome to Module two, safety: the safe direction, and the four safety rules.
The aim is for you to handle a firearm safely and confidently.

scenes.heading: Rules only work when applied
bullets: Rules alone can never prevent an accident
Accidents are prevented when rules are applied
Every safety rule begins with ALWAYS
Apply them consistently: they become automatic

lines.text: Safety rules in themselves can never prevent an accident.
Accidents are only prevented when the safety rules are applied.
You will notice that every safety rule begins with the word always.

lines: That is because you must always apply the safety rules when handling a firearm.

lines.text: If you consistently apply your safety rules, the actions will eventually become automatic.

lines: If you do not, your bad habits will become automatic, and that will lead to accidents.

scenes.definition: Ensures that in the event of an accidental discharge, no person shall be injured or killed.
lines: First, the term safe direction.
The purpose of a safe direction is to ensure that in the event of an accidental discharge, no person shall be injured or killed.

scenes.heading: Choosing a safe direction
bullets: The floor, the thickest wall, or both
45 degrees, where wall and floor meet
It must be able to stop the bullet
lines: When choosing a safe direction, use the floor or the thickest wall in the room, or both.
That means pointing the firearm at a 45 degree angle, at the point where the wall and floor meet.
That is to say, your safe direction must be able to stop the bullet.
And beware of ricochets!

scenes.caption: Beware of Ricochets
lines: In the event of an accidental discharge, the point of impact should be where the wall and the floor meet.
If the bullet strikes the floor first, it will then ricochet onto the wall.
If the bullet strikes the wall first, it will then ricochet onto the floor.
If the bullet strikes two surfaces, most of the energy of that speeding bullet will be removed.
There might still be enough energy for the bullet to come back at you.
But it is highly unlikely to have enough energy to cause serious harm or a fatal injury.

rule.text: ALWAYS keep the firearm pointed in a safe direction, away from people.

lines: Now the four safety rules, in order.
Rule one. Always keep the firearm pointed in a safe direction, away from people.
Be muzzle conscious: always know where the muzzle of the firearm is pointing.
Never allow your firearm to point at people, even when it is unloaded.

rule.text: ALWAYS keep your finger off the trigger until ready to fire.

lines: Rule two. Always keep your finger off the trigger until ready to fire.
Because the firearm is designed to fit a human hand, your finger will instinctively go to the trigger.
This is how most accidental discharges occur.

lines.text: Here is the trigger, where your finger will instinctively go.
You must make a conscious effort to keep your finger outside the trigger guard.
And keep it alongside the frame.

rule.text: ALWAYS treat a firearm as if it were loaded.

lines: Rule three. Always treat a firearm as if it were loaded.
If you always treat a firearm as if it is loaded, safe handling will become automatic.
And you will be demonstrating a positive attitude to those around you.

rule.text: ALWAYS know your target and what is beyond it.

lines: Rule four. Always know your target and what is beyond it.
A handgun is capable of projecting a bullet for distances up to 2 kilometres.
And you are liable for where that bullet stops.
So before firing the shot, know not only what your target is, but also where that bullet will come to rest.

scenes.question: Which is safety rule number two?
options: Treat a firearm as if it were loaded
Finger off the trigger until ready to fire
Know your target and what is beyond it
lines: The exam asks for the four safety rules in order.
So, which is safety rule number two?
reveal: Rule two: always keep your finger off the trigger until ready to fire.
Rule three is treat it as loaded, and rule four is know your target and what is beyond it.

scenes.question: Where should the point of impact be in an accidental discharge?
options: Where the wall and the floor meet
lines: In an accidental discharge, where should the point of impact be?
reveal: Where the wall and the floor meet.
A bullet that strikes two surfaces has most of its energy removed.

lines: So, a safe direction means no person is injured or killed in an accidental discharge.
Use the floor, the thickest wall, or both, so it can stop the bullet.
Rule one, keep it pointed in a safe direction, away from people.
Rule two, finger off the trigger until ready to fire.
Rule three, treat a firearm as if it were loaded.
And rule four, know your target and what is beyond it.
